correctness.rationale: Two exact full-array enumerators exhaust all 3^n ternary words for each 1<=n<=13, with independently derived direct-index and incremental recurrences. At n=13 the two enumerators return 1594311 profiles, twelve disjoint doubletons and support size exactly two for every doubleton. At 3<=n<=12 the map is injective. All coordinates are <=165 and exactly represented as uint8_t; word IDs are uint32_t, and all arrays are fully compared without hashing. The proof that a letter map sends equal decks to equal decks reduces every arbitrary q>=2 collision to a ternary collision while preserving a differing position; if the q-ary pair collectively uses three symbols, the ternary images must do so, contradicting the exhaustive ternary classification. Exact codebook counting follows by selecting one representative per fiber. The elementary n=2 exception and range boundaries are stated.

value.rationale: This determines the complete ambiguity structure at the natural nondegenerate binary k=3 threshold on every alphabet, rather than merely repeating the four binary pairs. Excluding extra three-letter fibers is a substantive issue because increasing alphabet size could create entirely new confusabilities. The result gives exact largest zero-error code sizes and all maximum labeled codebook counts, including the practically motivated four-symbol alphabet (67108840 codewords and 2^24 optimal codebooks). A finite exhaustive ternary lemma has direct all-alphabet consequences by a mathematical projection theorem; no claim about longer lengths is inflated.
